data.name: Amitri
data.gender_notes: Amitri is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words 'amita' meaning boundless and 'ri' meaning friend. The name Amitri carries the meaning “Boundless Friend” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amitri usually hope their child will grow to embody boundless friend and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes eternal friendship and boundless love.
data.etymology: Amitri belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Boundless Friend.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amitri total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Amitri" signifies an eternal friend or a friend who is unending, a bond that transcends the boundaries of time and space. In Indian culture, friendship is considered an essential and sacred bond that brings immense joy and happiness. The name is a beautiful way to honor and cherish this relationship.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Amitri" holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. The term 'amita' signifies the infinite and boundless nature of the Divine. The name is a reminder that the friendship we have with the Divine is also unending and eternal, and that the love and support of the Divine is always available to us. It encourages us to maintain a strong spiritual connection with the Divine, knowing that it is a constant presence in our lives, just like a true friend.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amitri: The radiant one, untouched by sorrow. Her name echoes the divine promise of infinite joy, free from the clutches of suffering.

vedic_reference.root_origin: Sanskrit root अमित् (amita) meaning 'immortal' + रि (ri) meaning 'friend'
vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads

historical_references.reference: Amitrya Chakravarti was a famous Hindu king who ruled the region of Eastern India known as Odisha from 1498 to 1541 AD. He is also known as Amitai and Amitrya Sen.
historical_references.context: Amitrya Chakravarti was a powerful ruler who expanded his kingdom through military conquests and alliances. He is considered one of the greatest kings of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty.

historical_references.reference: Amitra Mishra was a notable Jain scholar and poet who lived during the 15th century in India. He is also known by the name Amitasuri.
historical_references.context: Amitra Mishra made significant contributions to Jain literature with his works, including commentaries on various Jain scriptures and original poetic compositions.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Amitri continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Amitri from Hyderabad, India embodies the meaning of Amitri - "Boundless Friend". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
